# Limb Surgery
These work on arms, hands, legs and feet.
## Close Stump When a limb is torn off, the stump left behind bleeds [color=red]arterially[/color] until it's closed. Dressings, trauma kits and surgical line can't stop it. A tourniquet on the stump holds it until you can operate.
Operate on the part the limb came off: the [bold]chest[/bold] for an arm or leg, the [bold]arm[/bold] for a hand, the [bold]leg[/bold] for a foot. No incision is needed. 1. Clamp the stump artery with a [bold]hemostat[/bold].
2. Cauterize the stump shut with a [bold]cautery[/bold].
Closing the stump stops the bleeding for good. Reattaching the limb also closes its stump. Any tourniquet on the stump falls off onto the floor. A limb removed with surgery doesn't leave an open stump.
An open stump keeps bleeding even after the patient dies, so close it or tourniquet it before reviving them.
## Remove Limb Amputates a limb that can't be saved, such as one killed by a tourniquet left on too long. 1. [italic]Open the incision.[/italic]
2. Amputate the limb with a [bold]circular saw[/bold].
## Reattach Limb Attaches a severed limb, or a replacement. 1. [italic]Open the incision.[/italic]
2. Trim the dead tissue off the stump with a [bold]circular saw[/bold].
3. Prep the socket with a [bold]hemostat[/bold].
4. Attach the limb: hold it in your hand and use it on the patient. It has to be the right limb for the empty slot.
5. Cauterize the incision shut with a [bold]cautery[/bold].
## Replacement Limbs The [bold]limb printer[/bold] makes new limbs. It grows human limbs from biogenic matrix, and builds robotic limbs from metal sheets.
